sequence: The simulated coronary X-ray shows contrast filling the vessel and identifies the narrowed channel before cutting to a stent cross-section.
Three separate labelled examples show underexpansion, growth inside an opened stent and plaque within that tissue.
Tissue-growth and plaque labels switch at 41.033 and 44.900 seconds, nearest frames to the locked 41.018 and 44.907 second cue starts.
The clot is a separate example. A neutral emergency card follows without asking the viewer to diagnose the cause.
Two simulated coronary projections and separate IVUS and OCT views explain how clinicians assess the mechanism.
The balloon illustration follows the wire through an existing scaffold, then shows inflation, deflation and withdrawal. Repeat stenting is a separate option after mechanical assessment.
The report and scan illustrations lead to medicines and follow-up questions. The branded eight-second closing card gives references, production disclosure and the next episode.
audio_review_method: Full scene waveform comparison, with sampled closing silence and sole Alexander narration source.
modesty: Original diagrams and neutral icons. There are no depictions of real people or exposed anatomy.
scope: Long-master editorial review. Companions have separate review.
